__comment: Packet B7-2 / B7-2-followup, BUGS.md SKB-016: this Delay exposes both delayTime and feedback, so a runtime set_param can move either one. Two constants get pinned as a result. ExposedTail_BUS_TAIL_SECONDS is still the PESSIMISTIC compile-time upper bound (delayTime range max 2.0s x the 135 passes it takes feedback range max 0.95 to fall 60dB = 270.0) — kept only as documentation, no longer read by the countdown. The countdown itself is now armed from ExposedTail_bus_tail_seconds(p), the LIVE proc pinned right below it, which reads p.delayTime/p.feedback instead of their range maxima: with the authored defaults (0.25s / 0.3) it would compute a true tail of 0.25 x ceil(ln(0.001)/ln(0.3)) passes = 0.25 x 6 = 1.5s, exactly what the same patch bakes when nothing is exposed at all. That is the fix: exposing a tail parameter no longer costs anything until a game actually moves it.
